answer: A reputation ledger ties each agent's history to a non-transferable credential, so a new identity starts with no standing: a relic of past work cannot be cloned onto a fresh account. To gain weight, an identity must hold a refundable stake above a minimum ledge for a long vesting period, while a whisper network of peers attests to real interactions. An attacker creating thousands of fake identities must stake and wait for each one, plus earn peer attestation they cannot fake cheaply, so Sybil identities stay worthless while honest agents accumulate verifiable history.
